title: Two Pawns Against a Rook
summary: Improve the king before pushing: shoulder the defender away so the connected passers keep their winning timing.

nodes.question: Push the pawn, or improve the king first?
nodes.explanation: Black’s king on e8 and rook on c8 threaten to coordinate against f6 and g6. The white king must deny the defender access to f7.

branches.title: Use the king before advancing the passer
commentary: Begin in the source’s five-piece position after ...Ke8. The earlier rook sacrifice and pawn advance remain source context.
Kg8 preserves the win by preparing to meet a discovered rook check with Kf7.
Kd7+ leaves the eighth rank, uncovering Rc8’s check against the king on g8.
Kf7 shoulders the black king away from the f-pawn and keeps the g-pawn supported.
Kd6 is the illustrated attempt to approach the pawns from below.
g7 advances the passer only after the king has reached its useful square.
Ke5 continues Black’s approach. Rook sacrifices against the connected pawns still require care.
Kg6 protects g7 and f6 from the side, preserving the exact winning position. The branch stops at this checked setup rather than assuming a particular further rook move.
branches.explanation: Kg6 protects g7 and f6 from the side, preserving the exact winning position. The branch stops at this checked setup rather than assuming a particular further rook move.

branches.title: Push before shouldering the king
commentary: Compare the immediate pawn push while the king is still on h7. The source calls the resulting defense a draw, but the exact position is lost for White.
g7 loses the forced win and allows Black to force a win instead.
Kf7 blocks f6 and protects g8. That second role prevents White’s king from recapturing a rook on g8.
g8=Q+ is an independently replayed representative attempt to promote despite the blockade.
Rxg8 captures the queen and answers check. Kf7 protects the rook, so Kxg8 is illegal; Black retains a checked win.
branches.classification: source setup with independent alternative representative promotion and capture
branches.explanation: Rxg8 captures the queen and answers check. Kf7 protects the rook, so Kxg8 is illegal; Black retains a checked win.

branches.title: Step into the corner instead
commentary: The h8 corner also changes how White must meet the discovered rook check.
Kh8 gives away the win. From h8, the king cannot reach f7 in one move after the checking retreat.
Kd7+ uncovers the rook’s eighth-rank check. White has lost the favorable king route and the exact position is drawn.

exercises.prompt: Why is Kg8 stronger than g7?
exercises.answer: Kg8 lets White answer ...Kd7+ with Kf7, denying Black the king square needed to coordinate its rook against the pawns.

exercises.prompt: Why finish the selected line with Kg6?
exercises.answer: It protects both advanced pawns from the side and preserves the checked win while avoiding a careless pawn race.
